root.name: Sicilian Defense: Godiva Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Qb6

overview: In the Open Sicilian Black plays 4...Qb6 attacking the knight on d4 and b2. White commonly responds 5.Nb3 or 5.Ndb5 and Black has to be careful with his queen. The play is uneven: White develops quickly, Black has early queen activity and a Sicilian pawn structure.

white_ideas.idea: Retreat with Nb3 or jump to b5 and develop with Nc3
Use the tempo from the queen's outing to build the centre

black_ideas.idea: Pressure d4 and b2 with the queen
Develop with ...Nf6 and ...e6 and aim for the usual Sicilian counterplay

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian half-open c-file against a White e4 pawn

character.notes: An early queen sortie in a sharp Sicilian.

soundness.notes: Probably sound but gives White an easy lead.

structure.notes: Semi-open: the c-file is open for Black as in all Sicilians.

approach.notes: A rare Sicilian line but played at all levels.

character.reason: Early queen activity and sharp Sicilian lines.

soundness.reason: Black is not worse by force.

structure.reason: Sicilians are semi-open by the taxonomy.

approach.reason: Rare but not shunned by strong players.

plans.reason: Early queen and a development race.
